observation_summary: The method ArrayUtils.addAll throws an ArrayStoreException when attempting to concatenate arrays of incompatible types, which is an unhelpful runtime exception. The fix adds a try-catch block around the arraycopy operation to validate type compatibility and throw a more descriptive IllegalArgumentException.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a validation check (a try-catch block that inspects the component types of the arrays) to ensure that the operation is valid before or during execution. This is a classic case of adding a missing guard/validation check to handle an edge case (incompatible array types) that was previously causing an unhandled runtime exception.
evidence_used: The fix adds a try-catch block around System.arraycopy.
The catch block checks if type1.isAssignableFrom(type2) to validate compatibility.
The fix throws an IllegalArgumentException if the types are incompatible, which is a validation-based response.
The bug report states the goal is to throw an IllegalArgumentException instead of an ArrayStoreException.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix modifies the procedure, the core purpose is to add a validation check for input compatibility, which is the definition of Checking.
The fix does not change the method signature or the contract between components; it improves the internal validation of the existing contract.
